topic: AIPMM Certified Digital Product Manager (CDPM) exam preparation - the AIPMM credential for building exceptional digital products, covering Lean methodology, Jobs-To-Be-Done, Design Thinking, MVP and experimentation, agile delivery and roadmapping, product analytics and growth, and modern digital/AI-enabled product practices
exam_format: Approximately a 2-hour, ~120-question, proctored, closed-book multiple-choice exam. The exam is available through AIPMM's Authorized Training Partner (Productside) Digital Product Management self-study course, or via an AIPMM exam voucher. AIPMM does NOT publicly publish the passing score or official per-domain percentage weightings, so the domain weights in this course are editorial estimates that reflect the emphasis of the AIPMM digital product management body of knowledge, not AIPMM's official figures. Exam pricing varies by training partner and region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current AIPMM pricing.
question_types: multiple choice, single answer, exactly 4 options; scenario- and concept-based questions drawn from Lean, Jobs-To-Be-Done, Design Thinking, agile delivery, and product analytics
audience: Digital product managers, product owners, growth PMs, and PMs moving from traditional to digital/SaaS products who build software, platform, data, and AI-enabled products in iterative, agile environments. Candidates typically have 2-4 years of product or delivery experience. A natural next step after the AIPMM CPM (idea-to-launch foundations) and a strong companion to the technical and AI certifications in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Digital Product Management Foundations
domains.notes: What makes digital/software product management different from physical-product PM: continuous delivery vs one-time launch, the digital product life cycle, platform and data products, and the digital PM's role across discovery, delivery, and growth. Product vision, strategy, and outcome-orientation (outcomes over outputs). Operating models for digital products and the shift from project to product. Choosing the right operating stance for a described digital context.

domains.name: Customer Discovery, JTBD, and Design Thinking
domains.notes: Understanding users deeply: Jobs-To-Be-Done theory (functional, emotional, social jobs; job stories), Design Thinking (empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test), personas, journey maps, and continuous discovery habits. Problem framing and opportunity-solution trees. Turning qualitative insight into validated problems worth solving. Selecting the right discovery method for a described uncertainty.

domains.name: Lean, MVP, and Experimentation
domains.notes: Lean Startup and the build-measure-learn loop, hypotheses and riskiest-assumption testing, MVP types (concierge, Wizard of Oz, landing page, single-feature), and experiment design. A/B testing fundamentals, validated learning, and knowing when to pivot vs persevere. Distinguishing a genuine MVP/experiment from a mislabeled first release. Choosing the cheapest valid test for a described assumption is a recurring exam skill.

domains.name: Agile Delivery, Backlog, and Roadmapping
domains.notes: Agile and Scrum/Kanban for digital products, the product owner role, backlog creation and refinement, user stories and acceptance criteria, estimation, and prioritization frameworks (RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, Kano). Now-Next-Later and outcome-based roadmaps, value stream mapping, and continuous/iterative delivery. Managing dependencies and technical debt at a PM level. Choosing the right prioritization or delivery approach for a described constraint.

domains.name: Product Analytics, Metrics, and Growth
domains.notes: Instrumenting digital products and choosing the right metrics: North Star metric, AARRR/pirate metrics, activation, retention and cohort analysis, funnels, and guardrail metrics. Distinguishing vanity from actionable metrics, setting targets, and running growth experiments. Pricing/monetization and PLG (product-led growth) basics for digital products. Interpreting a described metric movement and choosing the correct next action.

domains.name: Digital Product Design, Emerging Tech, and Responsible AI
domains.notes: UX and interaction fundamentals a digital PM must partner on, accessibility, and design systems at a working level. Building AI/ML-enabled features responsibly: when to use ML, evaluating probabilistic/non-deterministic outputs, data and privacy considerations, and ethics/trust and safety. Security, compliance, and platform/API and integration thinking for modern products. Choosing the right approach for an AI-enabled or platform feature given a described risk or constraint.

extra_guidance: AIPMM CDPM is the digital/software-focused companion to the CPM and the more modern, hands-on of the two: it is a real ~2-hour, ~120-question proctored closed-book exam covering Lean, Jobs-To-Be-Done, Design Thinking, agile delivery, product analytics, and increasingly AI-enabled product work - which maps perfectly to this catalog's AI/tech audience. CRITICAL accuracy note: AIPMM does NOT publish official per-domain percentage weightings or the passing score, so present the domain NAMES as objective areas but mark the weights as editorial estimates (leading '~'), never as AIPMM's official figures - state this where weights appear. This is a decision-and-method exam: the real skill is choosing the right discovery method, MVP/experiment, prioritization framework, or metric for a described digital-product scenario, so practice questions MUST be predominantly scenario-based with plausible distractors and 'BEST / cheapest valid / MOST appropriate / FIRST' framing, mixed with clean concept/term-matching (JTBD job types, MVP types, AARRR stages, RICE vs WSJF). Use the exact vocabulary of each framework (build-measure-learn, riskiest assumption, North Star metric, opportunity-solution tree, acceptance criteria) rather than generic slang. Lean into the AI/digital angle in the emerging-tech domain and in examples throughout (evaluating a non-deterministic AI feature, choosing metrics for an AI product, an MVP for an ML capability) since it differentiates this course and fits the catalog - but keep the CORE anchored to AIPMM's digital PM body of knowledge, not deep ML theory. Frame the credential honestly as 'exam-focused preparation' - never promise a pass, guarantee, or 'first attempt' success (Udemy compliance). Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with time-management strategy for ~120 questions in ~2 hours plus framework-elimination guidance. Do NOT invent AIPMM's official passing score or exact fee; present the fee as approximate and advise verifying current AIPMM pricing. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor cloud terms (AWS/Azure/GCP) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
